title: Activation staffing surge calculator & KPI sheet
content:
Purpose:
This working sheet pairs a lightweight FTE calculator with action-oriented KPIs and an explicit decision matrix for first-72h launch operations. Use to staff rotational coverage, plan surge runways, and codify go/no-go rollback thresholds.

Quick summary (how to use):
- Populate 'Inputs' with your expected traffic profile and latency targets.
- Review the 'Baseline operator load' assumptions.
- The calculator outputs recommended on-call FTEs and a 0-72h escalation plan.
- Review KPI thresholds and apply to canary or beta traffic before full ramp.

ASSUMPTIONS (editable):
- Average requests per active user per day: 5
- Peak-to-median ratio: 3.2
- Mean tokens per request: 120
- Average tokens/sec per GPU slot: 200
- Operator average triage time per incident: 18 minutes
- Escalation step runbook time (SRE): 35 minutes

Inputs (required):
- projected_daily_active_users: 15000
- expected_canary_pct: 5
- expected_ramp_hours: 12
- target_p99_latency_ms: 450
- acceptable_error_rate_pct: 0.6

Calculator steps (spreadsheet cells described for implementation):
1) Expected RPS median = (projected_daily_active_users * requests_per_user) / 86400
2) Peak RPS = median * peak_to_median_ratio
3) Token throughput = Peak RPS * mean_tokens_per_request
4) GPU slots needed = ceil(Token throughput / tokens_per_gpu_slot * safety_margin(1.25))
5) Operator FTE baseline = ceil((estimated_incident_count_per_hour * avg_triage_minutes/60) / productive_hours_per_FTE)

Sample output (example values with current inputs):
- median RPS: 0.87
- peak RPS: 2.78
- token throughput peak (tokens/s): 333
- GPU slots recommended (w/25% buffer): 2
- baseline operator FTE: 1.2 -> round to 2 people (day shift)
- on-call rotational FTE for 0-72h surge: 3 people (12-hour shifts)

Operator load & roles (recommended rota):
- Launch commander (product-ops lead) - 08:00-20:00 first 72h
- Ops engineer (service health) - 24/7 on-call first 72h (primary)
- SRE escalation - 08:00-00:00 first 72h (secondary on-call)
- Solutions engineer - daytime triage and customer comms

KPI sheet (operational thresholds - map to alerts):
- latency_p95_ms: green <= 300, amber 300-600, red >600
- latency_p99_ms: green <= 500, amber 500-900, red >900
- error_rate_pct: green <= 0.2, amber 0.2-1.0, red >1.0
- queue_depth_requests: green <= 50, amber 50-200, red >200
- dropped_requests_pct: green <= 0.05, amber 0.05-0.5, red >0.5
- cost_per_1000_requests_usd: set monitoring alert if > expected_baseline * 1.4

Action matrix (automated + human):
- If p99 > amber threshold for 3 consecutive 1-minute buckets: alert ops engineer, add a hot patch route to lower-cost model variant, throttle nonessential clients.
- If error_rate enters red: immediate canary rollback to previous model variant and notify Launch commander.
- If queue_depth > red and GPU slots at max: spin additional dedicated nodes (if capacity) OR enable staged failover (degrade to cached responses) and notify SRE.

Go/No-Go & rollback signals (explicit):
- Hard rollback triggers (execute within 10m): sustained error_rate > 2% for 5 min OR p99 > 2x target for 10 min despite autoscaling attempts.
- Soft rollback triggers (discuss within 15m): p99 > amber and customer-impacting errors in top-10 requests.

72-hour playbook highlights (run order):
T-minus 2h: final traffic probe (1% traffic for 15 minutes), confirm p95/p99 within amber bounds, validate alerting routes.
T+0-6h: tight monitoring cadence: 15m war-room syncs, shift handoff template, customer comms staging.
T+6-24h: expand probe to 10% if stable, re-evaluate operator FTE and spin additional day shift if load > 1.2x forecast.
T+24-72h: move from minute cadence to hourly if signals stable; migrate to normal on-call by 72h.

Communication templates (snippets):
- Incident slack banner: [LAUNCH] {short_desc} | p99={value}ms | action={rollback|scale|mitigate} | commander={name}
- Customer advisory (if degraded): short explanation, ETA for fix, workaround, contact mailbox.

Unresolved questions / follow-ups:
- Confirm runbook automation for hot fallback variant swap (PR reference above).
- Add cost burn alert for dedicated pools (threshold currently manual).
- Confirm KMS access for private telemetry exports in Private deployments.

Version history:
- v0.1 2025-02-10 initial working draft (Asha)
- v0.2 2025-03-15 added operator rota and finer thresholds (Evan, Priya)

Notes to editors:
- This is an operational working artifact intended for product-ops and SRE pairing. Keep conservative thresholds for first 3 launches and iterate afterward.

End of sheet.
